entries.name: A Bugesera king flees
entries.place_and_era: Bugesera to Rwanda. The source sets this in the late seventeenth century.
entries.attested: The chapter says the Baganwa rose against Bugesera. King Nsoro Nyabarega had to flee to Rwanda.
entries.unknown: It names a king, not a whole court or people in flight. The source keeps two ruler names open and says less is known of Burundi.
entries.next_step: This is a source lead. Resolve the land or home-loss unit before any case assessment.

entries.name: A chief and the rule of a district in the Udayendiram charter
entries.place_and_era: South Asia. The text names the district as Vishnuraja. The date of the event remains unknown.
entries.attested: The charter reports the defeat of a chief and an order to leave. It also reports Pallava rule over the district.
entries.unknown: An order does not show that the chief left. The fate and rights of residents and the duration of rule remain unknown.
entries.next_step: Check how the atlas shows this case with an unknown date.

entries.name: A claim of captives at site 1Pi61
entries.place_and_era: Pickens County, Alabama. Dye places the burials in the Late Woodland period. Exact dates remain unknown.
entries.attested: Dye reports that other researchers read the burial treatment as a sign of captives. Their view concerns people buried at this site.
entries.unknown: Burials alone do not show where these people came from or how they reached this site. The report does not establish slave status or forced labor.
entries.next_step: Define the captive claim and the control over people that it implies. Keep this view distinct from proof of transport.

entries.name: A disputed model of moves into New York
entries.place_and_era: New York and central Pennsylvania. One model placed the move around 900. A later version put it before the sixth century. Neither is an adopted event date.
entries.attested: Keener reports a model by Snow. In it, groups moved north, fought and drove earlier residents away. He also describes a view that the people developed there. He gives evidence that changed the proposed dates.
entries.unknown: The migration and forced moves remain disputed. Pots and village patterns do not settle who moved or why. We have not read the original debate papers.
entries.next_step: Check the move and land claims against the cited studies and the view that people developed there.

entries.name: A grant in Sylhet
entries.place_and_era: Sylhet, seventh century CE in this account. The issuer and exact year remain unnamed.
entries.attested: The chapter describes a land gift meant to extend cultivation into a forest tract.
entries.unknown: The forest claim does not prove that no one used the land. The exact recipients and actual effects remain unknown.
entries.next_step: Find prior use and the effect of this grant. Keep it apart from the later Chandra grant.

entries.name: A mountain town: defeat and later departure
entries.place_and_era: North America, in the source account. The date and exact place are unknown.
entries.attested: The 1896 English account by Cushing says warriors defeated a mountain town. They spared some people from cellars and took them into Black Corn kin. Those people later left with the southern group.
entries.unknown: The account does not prove that these acts took place. It gives no firm date or modern site. It does not show if people had to join the later journey or lost their homes for good. Its Black people label does not set a modern racial identity.
entries.next_step: Find evidence for the time, place and later journey. Keep the cause of that journey unknown.

entries.name: A report of brief loss of rule at Pandua
entries.place_and_era: Pandua in Bengal. Eaton gives 1353 as context for this invasion. Exact dates for the loss of rule remain unknown.
entries.attested: Eaton reports that Firuz Tughluq drove Shams al-Din Ilyas Shah from Pandua for a time. He failed to annex Bengal.
entries.unknown: The text does not establish removal of civilians or long-term control. The later invasion is a separate question.
entries.next_step: Define the brief change in control at Pandua. Keep it distinct from the later invasion and from the coin traces at Chhota Pandua.

entries.name: A report of new rule in Kamata and Kamrup
entries.place_and_era: Kamata and western Assam (Kamrup). Eaton gives 1494 as campaign context. Exact dates and bounds remain unknown.
entries.attested: Eaton reports that Husain Shah invaded and annexed these tracts. The claim concerns a change of rule.
entries.unknown: The report does not establish civilian removal or resettlement. The length of control remains unclear. It does not define all of modern Assam.
entries.next_step: Define the tracts and the change in control in this report. Keep this process distinct from Tai-Ahom settlement.

entries.name: A report of the removal of Ho-Chunk in Wisconsin
entries.place_and_era: The Wisconsin Driftless Area. The authors report removal in the 1840s. The exact dates remain unknown.
entries.attested: Theler and Boszhardt report the removal of many Ho-Chunk. This question concerns their loss of residence.
entries.unknown: The text leaves each affected group and its next place unclear. The agents and the separate moves remain unknown. The old records that the authors cite remain unverified here.
entries.next_step: Define the affected tracts and the link to the broader Old Northwest case. Keep the reported removal as an open question.

entries.name: A royal report about the town of Pithumda
entries.place_and_era: South Asia. The reported act has no fixed calendar date.
entries.attested: A translated royal text says the king ploughed down a named town with asses.
entries.unknown: The act and its effects remain unverified. The fate of residents, land rights and length of control are unknown.
entries.next_step: The source assessment is saved and an atlas draft is next, with the reported act and unknown outcomes kept distinct.

entries.name: Abok loses rule
entries.place_and_era: Koc. The source gives no exact date for the overthrow.
entries.attested: Jonam traditions in the chapter say Luo under Daca overthrew Abok. Koc split into three states.
entries.unknown: The chapter gives a political outcome. It does not establish eviction or an exact act date. A named tradition adds no second witness here.
entries.next_step: This is a candidate for study. Resolve the unit and its limits before any case assessment.

entries.name: Afghan refugees received lands and towns in Bengal
entries.place_and_era: Bengal after the defeat by Babur in 1526. That defeat is date context. Exact dates for refuge and grants remain unknown.
entries.attested: Eaton reports that Nasir al-Din Nusrat Shah gave refuge to defeated Afghans. His cited note reports lands and towns endowed to these refugees.
entries.unknown: The report does not name each grant or its bounds. It does not establish harm to prior residents. Modern Afghan or Pashtun labels do not identify this group.
entries.next_step: Define the refugee group and the lands and towns in the report. Keep the grants and refuge as one open question.

entries.name: Afrin occupation and property loss
entries.place_and_era: Afrin, northern Syria; from 2018

entries.name: Ahom loss and return of rule
entries.place_and_era: The later Ahom realm. The account reports defeat in 1662 and a return to rule a few years later.
entries.attested: Terwiel reports an Ahom defeat in 1662. Muslim invaders defeated them. Ahom rule resumed a few years later.

entries.next_step: Trace effects on residents and the extent of the changed rule. Keep this later sequence distinct from early conquests.

entries.name: Contested use at Mulberry Creek

entries.next_step: Define the disputed uses and any change in access or control at this site.

entries.name: Cottonwood Wash archaeological comparison

entries.name: Crow Creek attack and residence loss
entries.place_and_era: Crow Creek. The source places village life in the 1300s. The date of the attack remains unknown.
entries.attested: Willey describes an attack at Crow Creek. He links burned lodges to the loss of village life, homes and defense. He considers that some people escaped. He proposes that escaped villagers returned, or people with ties to them came, to bury the dead. He also reports later ceremonies at the site.
entries.unknown: The attackers and the fates of all survivors remain unknown. Willey does not fix the dates of each fire or prove later village residence. He gives two possible causes for the upper bone layer. The detailed methods behind his summaries remain unread.
entries.next_step: Keep this source account with the same Crow Creek record. Retain the unknown fire dates, later village use and survivor destinations.

entries.name: Daur removal from the Amur
entries.place_and_era: Amur region and Nonni valley; source reports 1653–1654
entries.attested: A book reports a state order to destroy homes and crops, then Daur flight to the Nonni valley.
entries.unknown: The text does not show if all ordered fires occurred or which homes they affected.
entries.next_step: Review how this removal relates to other Amur histories before a separate atlas case.

entries.name: Denbigh change: did people have to leave?
entries.place_and_era: Alaska, near the Bering Sea and Arctic coasts. The source gives broad age ranges, not a firm event date.
entries.attested:
A 2018 state report says a migration with Denbigh culture displaced or replaced earlier people. It leaves that choice open. It also describes later continuity with Choris.

The Raghavan study supports continuity among some sampled groups in Canada and Greenland. Its results do not resolve this Denbigh claim.

Anderson reports Ipiutak homes and camps at Cape Krusenstern. He says that people later left those houses. This does not settle the earlier Denbigh claim.
entries.unknown: The report does not link a human act to a loss of homes or land. Changes in tools or DNA do not prove that people had to leave.
entries.next_step: Selected Cape chapters now give context. They cover chronology, Birnirk and Ipiutak, with figures and plates. They do not settle the earlier Denbigh claim. The Oxford chapter remains unread because access is blocked. Seek evidence that links a human act to loss of homes, land use or control.

entries.name: Did these groups merge or leave?

entries.name: What links Ipiutak warfare and later change?
entries.place_and_era: Northern and western Alaska. The source gives broad age ranges, not a firm event date.
entries.attested:
The 2018 report describes violent injuries. It also reports later population replacement. It does not link those injuries to one forced loss of homes or land.

Anderson reports houses, camps and later house abandonment at Cape Krusenstern. He also describes resource use. House 30 burned. Three partly burned skeletons lay beneath the fallen wood.

Anderson reports a possible earlier wound in one adult. He interprets the positions of the children as possible attempts to dig down and escape.
entries.unknown:
The report also notes trade and some intermarriage. Ipiutak is an archaeological label, not proof of one modern people. Dates and the causes of change remain unclear.

The cause of the fire is unknown. The chapter does not establish an attack, a forced move or the fate of the whole community.

Raghavan discusses Dorset and Thule farther east. That text reports no massacre evidence. It does not rule out the Ipiutak injuries.
entries.next_step: Keep the house fire and later replacement claim separate. Ask whether a source links a human act to loss of homes, land use or control. The Ipiutak chapter and its figures and plates give context. They do not resolve that link.

entries.name: Where did Jaki extend his rule?

entries.name: Whistling Elk burned lodges

entries.name: Who sought refuge by the Nile?

entries.next_step: This is a candidate for study. Resolve the unit and its limits before any case assessment.

entries.name: Bhir lane walls and public access
entries.place_and_era: Small lanes at Bhir Mound, Taxila, with the west end of Lane 2 as an example. The date remains unknown.

entries.name: Bhir sack and possible loss of use
entries.place_and_era: The West Group at Bhir Mound, Taxila. Marshall places the sack in the early second century BCE. The date remains unassigned here.

entries.name: Reported loss of Murrelet-point fort
entries.place_and_era: Murrelet-point fort in a Tlingit oral account. Its modern site and the date of the attack remain unknown.

entries.name: Reported loss of village rights in Sonpur

entries.name: Sri Lanka: proposed Naga arrival in the Iron Age

entries.name: Vijitanagara: the text says people fled from the river bank to this city

entries.name: Vijitanagara: the text says the king took the city in a siege

entries.next_step: Keep the reported siege as one research record. Its effects on residents remain unknown.
